'''Mark Allen Ludwig''' (August 5, 1958 – 2011) was an American physicist. He was the author of books on [[computer virus]]es and [[artificial life]].  He died from cancer at age 51.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=http://www.en-genius.net/site/zones/lowpowerZONE/editorial_opinion/lpwre_100112 |title=Richard Feynman Preserved by Homomorphic Filtering |website=www.en-genius.net |access-date=13 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130908004520/http://www.en-genius.net/site/zones/lowpowerZONE/editorial_opinion/lpwre_100112 |archive-date=8 September 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Education ==
Ludwig spent less than two years as an undergraduate at [[MIT]], but was reputedly still able to get into the Physics doctorate program at [[Caltech]] on the basis of recommendation letters from his past MIT teachers where he was a classmate of [[Stephen Wolfram]] in [[Richard Feynman]]'s course on advanced mathematical methods for physics.<ref name=":0" />

==Work==
Ludwig had his own virus-writing periodical, ''Computer Virus Developments Quarterly''. He also held the ''First International Virus Writing Competition'', which promised a monetary reward of $200 for the creator of the smallest [[MS-DOS]]-based, parasitic file infecter.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/03/20/magazine/sunday-march-20-1994-the-gotcha-virus.html|title=SUNDAY, MARCH 20, 1994; The Gotcha! Virus|date=20 March 1994|work=[[The New York Times]]|accessdate=4 January 2015}}</ref>

His ''Little Black Book of Computer Viruses'' fully describes a sophisticated MS-DOS executable virus.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ebookrally.com/download-book/3990532/the-little-black-book-of-computer-viruses|title=Description|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613234818/https://ebookrally.com/download-book/3990532/the-little-black-book-of-computer-viruses|archive-date=2018-06-13|access-date=|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.virusbtn.com/conference/vb94/VB94report.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081117021000/http://www.virusbtn.com/conference/vb94/VB94report.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 17, 2008 |title=Search results |website=google.com}} {{Better source needed|date=August 2022}}</ref> The second, ''Giant Black Book of Computer Viruses'' contains the source code of two [[UNIX]] companion viruses written in [[C language|C]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iwar.org.uk/comsec/resources/plausibility.htm|title=The Plausibility of UNIX Virus Attacks|author=Wanja Eric Naef|publisher=Iwar.org.uk|accessdate=4 January 2015}}</ref> In his book ''Computer Viruses, Artificial Life and Evolution: The Little Black Book of Computer Viruses'' he argued for [[intelligent design]]. The book was criticized by biologist [[Gert Korthof]] for making errors and incorrect statements about evolutionary biology.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://wasdarwinwrong.com/korthof77.htm|title=Mark A. Ludwig: Computer Viruses, Artificial Life and Evolution.|last=Korthof|first=Gert|date=|website=wasdarwinwrong.com|access-date=2018-06-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://wasdarwinwrong.com/feedback/Reply_Mark_Ludwig.htm|title=Mark Ludwig's Reply: Intelligent Design Theorist - Fact or Fiction?|last=Ludwig|first=Mark|date=June 10, 2006|website=wasdarwinwrong.org|access-date=June 13, 2018}}</ref>
